text:
Cole Perfetti has stopped being the Jets' useful middle-six piece and become one of the people the offense runs through. He's playing 18:17 a night, up from 15:37 last season, and he's on the ice for 90% of Winnipeg's power-play chances after sitting at half of them a year ago. Nine of his 19 points in 21 games have come on the power play, which tells you where the jump starts.

Some of it is real and some of it is borrowed. His own chances are up to 1.48 expected goals per 60 (expected goals measure the quality of the looks he gets), well above last season's 1.08, and he has actually finished a bit below that. The borrowed part is around him: the Jets have scored about three goals more than their chances deserve with him on the ice. His recent run, a five-game point streak with six assists, has come with fewer shots (one in the Dallas game, none against New Jersey). Watch whether the shot volume comes back, because that's the part of this breakout we'd trust most.
